title: Assemble the reference list into the manuscript and reconcile citations both ways

Marine Policy will want those either obtained at source or explicitly flagged. And apply the four wrong filename years recorded in REFERENCES-verified.md - do not cite any of them from the filename.

Do after the literature task, which will add entries. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md
notes:
ASSEMBLY SOURCE IS REFERENCES.md, not REFERENCES-verified.md.

REFERENCES.md: 20 entries, four sections (published/peer-reviewed, legal and regulatory instruments, statistical metadata and web sources, notes on construction). Harvard alphabetical. Coverage checked 2026-08-17: every surname cited in the manuscript resolves to an entry - BAPPENAS, Beukering, Fenichel, Gacutan, Giyanto, Hoberg, IDEEA Group, Jannah, MMAF, Muttaqin, Rahayu, Rinaldi, Ruitenbeek, Samonte, Tasriah, United Nations, Wuwung. No missing entries found.

REFERENCES-verified.md is NOT the list: its own title scopes it 'for the introduction' and it holds only 9 entries. It is a QA companion, and its three warning sections must be APPLIED during assembly rather than assembled: (1) four filename years are wrong - Rinaldi is 2025, OceanPanel is 2020, IDEEA is 2021, SEEA-EA is a 2024 imprint of a 2021 adoption; (2) the not-citable list - ADB slide deck, ASEAN snapshot, MFAT report, and PermenKP 18/2025 citable by number and 3 Nov 2025 enactment only; (3) the remaining hole, tracked separately as ibei-0vx.

Both directions reconcile: 30 entries, every one cited at least once, every in-text author-date resolving to an entry. Five unsuffixed 'MMAF, 2022' citations resolved to 2022a (the Gili Matra pilot) and one 'BAPPENAS 2025' to 2025a. MMAF 2022b/2022c, Wulandari and Jannah 2023 and Yulianto et al. 2012 had no in-text citation and now carry one. title: Source composite-indicator methodology literature and engage contradicting work in section 9
description:
Live issue L4 (referee M9, unfixed). Sections 8-9 cite only three external works, all supportive: United Nations et al. 2024, Rahayu et al. 2024, Gacutan et al. 2022. REFERENCES-verified.md independently records the cause as 'the remaining hole': no composite-indicator methodology literature exists in the project document set - no OECD/JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators, no Ocean Health Index or comparable, nothing on weighting-scheme sensitivity, PCA-derived weights, or imputation inside composite indices.

Why it matters: without it the Introduction cannot establish that the IBEI's construction is a recognised class of problem rather than an idiosyncratic Indonesian one, which is the move that licenses the novelty claim. Section 8.3's variance-weighting argument has the same exposure.

Do this FIRST: it is the only live item needing new reading, it may ADD words, and the word-count cut plan must be built knowing its cost. Not blocked by the no-agency-engagement constraint.

Done when: composite-indicator methodology literature sourced from outside the project folder, and at least two works brought into section 9 that can be read AGAINST the conclusion. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md
close_reason: Satisfied by v2. Six composite-indicator methodology works sourced from outside the project folder and brought into the discussion: Nardo et al. 2008 (the OECD/JRC handbook, on imputation, weighting and aggregation as the three choices that most move a ranking), Halpern et al. 2012 and Frazier et al. 2016 (Ocean Health Index, and its 18.5% gapfilled-score disclosure with the recommendation that gapfilling be tracked from the outset), Paruolo et al. 2013 and Becker et al. 2017 (nominal against effective weight, and the correlation-ratio test that would settle it), and Ravallion 2012 (mashup indices). At least two are read AGAINST the conclusion as required: Ravallion doubts the value added of such indices relative to monitoring the components, and Paruolo/Becker undercut the article's own weight arithmetic by separating nominal from effective weight. Section 5.4 is built as 'three readings that would lead elsewhere'. The 'remaining hole' recorded in REFERENCES-verified.md is closed.

description:

WHAT STILL BLOCKS THE PASS:

[CONTESTED DENOMINATOR] fell from 6 to 2 in the citation-check pass, which reduced it to a single meaning (bears-on versus supplies) and restated the weight-loading question as prose. The two survivors are the definition in 3.6 and the use in 4.2.

WORD BUDGET, which is the real constraint. Body prose is 9,995 against a 10,000 ceiling: 5 words of headroom. Deleting all 33 main-text tags outright recovers 52 words, giving 9,943 and 57 words of headroom for the replacement prose. That is about 1.7 words per tag on average, so this cannot be done by appending a clause to every flagged sentence.

What makes it feasible: most tags sit on sentences whose prose already carries the hedge -- 'is stated in no source', 'no reconciliation is published', 'no obtained document evidences' -- where conversion is deletion, not rewriting. All 11 [ASSUMPTION] instances are of that kind. A minority, concentrated in [EVIDENCE GAP], need new wording and must be paid for by trimming elsewhere in the same section.
